support-irrigation.label: Support watering during stress

aspects.Purpose: Respond to unusually dry weather, heat or plant stress.
aspects.Amount: LIFE: Not specified in this source. MR2: Not specified in this source. El Triguero reports 50 L/plant/event as a site-specific emergency practice.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: LIFE: monitor forecasts and plant condition; prolonged lack of rain or widespread yellow/dry symptoms can prompt watering. El Triguero reports monthly emergency watering.
aspects.Applicable period: When the stated conditions occur; no universal seasonal calendar.
aspects.Age and stock: May overlap the field establishment years and maintenance. No general dose by plant age or automatic stopping age is supplied.

aspects.Purpose: Recurring water during difficult seasonal conditions.
aspects.Amount: LIFE traditional/Cocoon: 15 L/plant/event; IND: 10 L/plant/event. “SAD”: approximately 15 L/plant/event. Carob examples have their own doses.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: Traditional/Cocoon/IND: monthly. “SAD”: tank filling triggers discharge; the project describes about every three weeks, not a guaranteed interval.
aspects.Applicable period: LIFE traditional/Cocoon/IND: July–September inclusive. SAD calendar season: Not specified in this source.
aspects.Age and stock: LIFE method passages discuss the first field year. Carob examples include the first two summers; this does not establish a universal stopping age.
aspects.Limitations: The first-year water-network estimate (about 40 L/plant, around 12.5 L/event) is a storage-planning estimate, separate from method-specific schedules. Seasonal totals cannot supply a dose by themselves.

nursery-irrigation.label: Nursery watering
nursery-irrigation.description: Before field planting, maintain suitable substrate moisture and adapt irrigation to the growing stage, stock, climate and hardening programme. LIFE NIEBLAS documents a project nursery regime; the carob handbook does not prescribe a universal numerical nursery dose.

aspects.Amount: LIFE NIEBLAS: approximately 0.3 L/plant/event as an average calculated from 30 L for 100 plants. Carob handbook: Not specified in this source.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: LIFE: twice weekly. Carob: frequent irrigation during growth; more intense, spaced applications during hardening, adapted to weather.
aspects.Applicable period: Nursery growth and preconditioning before planting; no universal calendar.
aspects.Age and stock: Nursery one-season stock (1+0) and two-season grafted stock (1+1) have different programmes. These ages are not years since field planting.
aspects.Limitations: A 1 L or 3 L pot is container capacity, not water dose. Up to 10% leaching describes drainage, not litres per plant. A batch average is not a measured individual dose.

nonproductive-demonstration.label: Non-productive demonstration
nonproductive-demonstration.description: The activity may not give the beneficiary an economic benefit; business participation may not become direct and exclusive modernization of those firms.

open-participation.label: Open and transparent participation
open-participation.description: Participation must be open to entitled entities. Limited places require objective transparent selection documented in the operation report; membership of the beneficiary cannot be an entry condition.

public-results.label: Publish demonstration and results
public-results.description: Publish activity information online from its start and results as they emerge; retain the information at least three years after final aid payment.

territory-link.label: Clear link to the LEADER territory
territory-link.description: The demonstration needs a clear unequivocal link to the zone; an application/study area larger than its territory is excluded.

complete-operation.label: Usable results on completion
complete-operation.description: Partial or phased operations are excluded if results cannot be applied or disseminated when the funded operation finishes.

al20-population.label: Settlement population
al20-population.description: Source criterion AT.3 for non-productive Line 3 operations. AT.3.1: settlement population below median municipal population of its LEADER zone, using INE 2023 data (10 points). AT.3.2: below median municipal population of Andalusia, using INE 2023 (8).

al20-local-needs.label: Prioritized local-strategy needs
al20-local-needs.description: Source criterion CO.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. CO.1.1: one prioritized EDLL need (10 points); CO.1.2: two (12); CO.1.3: three or more (15). Starred needs depend on the strategy.

al20-territorial-balance.label: Territorial and economic balance
al20-territorial-balance.description: Source criterion RD.5 for non-productive Line 3 operations. RD.5.1: support to municipalities with fewer businesses than the mean of the LEADER zone (15 points).

al20-renewable-energy.label: Renewable-energy equipment
al20-renewable-energy.description: Source criterion CC.2 for non-productive Line 3 operations. CC.2.1 lists solar collectors, photovoltaic panels, thermosiphons, wind turbines, biomass boilers, heat accumulators, aerothermal equipment, biofuels, blue hydrogen, liquefied natural gas or similar (5 points). These source examples are not an independent environmental endorsement.

al20-sustainable-mobility.label: Sustainable mobility
al20-sustainable-mobility.description: Source criterion CC.7 for non-productive Line 3 operations. CC.7.1: green-energy collective transport (1 point); CC.7.2: electric-vehicle charging points (4); CC.7.3: municipal pedestrianization, cycle lanes/parking, park-and-ride parking, high-occupancy vehicle encouragement or other measures in a sustainable-mobility plan (4). Family maximum 5.

al20-gender-leisure.label: Leisure with a gender perspective
al20-gender-leisure.description: Source criterion IG.8 for non-productive Line 3 operations. IG.8.1: spaces/infrastructure for women (2 points); IG.8.2: activities demanded by women in EDLL (2); IG.8.3: sociocultural activities fostering women creativity (2); IG.8.4: sport with a gender perspective (2). Family maximum 2.

al20-womens-associations.label: Participation and associations among women
al20-womens-associations.description: Source criterion IG.11 for non-productive Line 3 operations. IG.11.1: rural women associations/federations (2 points); IG.11.2: association maintenance/equipment (2); IG.11.3: association activities (2); IG.11.4: association networks (2); IG.11.5: dissemination about associations, especially young women/women with disabilities (1); IG.11.6: women participation in underrepresented sectors (1). Family maximum 2. IG.11.7 continues on PDFpage 18.

al20-accessibility.label: Adaptive and inclusive structures
al20-accessibility.description: Source criterion DRI.3 for non-productive Line 3 operations. DRI.3.1: facilities/processes adapted to disability limitations beyond statutory minima, or adapted by the operation (3 points); DRI.3.2: staff training for vulnerable groups/people at risk of exclusion, including training by the operation (2); DRI.3.3: addresses related specific EDLL needs (1). Family maximum 4.

al20-rural-youth.label: Positive action for rural youth
al20-rural-youth.description: Source criterion JR.3 for non-productive Line 3 operations. JR.3.1: courses for youth skills/employability (4 points); JR.3.2: dual vocational education or official youth placements (4); JR.3.3: return of recently qualified young people within 12 months of completing medium/higher education and labour-market incorporation in the zone (3); JR.3.4: awareness/training on youth contribution to local development (2); JR.3.5: rural youth leisure (4); JR.3.6: associations/participation and quality of life (4). Family maximum 4. Further rows continue on PDFpage 19.

al20-innovation.label: Local-strategy innovation
al20-innovation.description: Source criterion IN.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. IN.1.1: sector considered innovative in EDLL (0.02 points); IN.1.2: innovative theme (2.49); IN.1.3: innovative aspect (2.49). Family maximum 5. All refer to starred strategy definitions.

al20-heritage-value.label: Enhancement of rural heritage
al20-heritage-value.description: Source criterion PT.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. PT.1.1: natural/monumental/architectural/artistic heritage enhanced for subsequent use through physical work, training, dissemination or awareness (13 points); PT.1.2: traditional trades/gastronomic specialties identified in EDLL (7); PT.1.3: other heritage action identified as of interest in EDLL (2). Family maximum 15.

al20-cooperation.label: Promoter cooperation and associations
al20-cooperation.description: Source criterion PS.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. PS.1.1: first/second-level cooperative membership (4 points); PS.1.2: associations/entities with an EDLL cross-cutting objective (4); PS.1.3: associations/entities promoting rural/endogenous development in the zone (8). Family maximum 12.

al20-new-beneficiary.label: Previous LEADER beneficiary status
al20-new-beneficiary.description: Source criterion PS.3 for non-productive Line 3 operations. PS.3.1: natural/legal persons who have never received aid in previous LEADER calls (1 point).

al20-local-services.label: Access to quality local services
al20-local-services.description: Source criterion SP.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. SP.1.1: new proximity services for the general population (5 points); SP.1.2: improved existing services (4); SP.1.3: proximity services for dependent people (1). Family maximum 5.

retama-sphaerocarpa.label: Retama
retama-sphaerocarpa.description: Broom-form shrub with slender green shoots and yellow axillary flower clusters. The UAL account places it in retama scrub, sometimes pioneering ramblas, across varied substrates.
retama-sphaerocarpa.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Slender, flexible grey-green shoots, losing their small leaves early; small yellow pea flowers in short lateral clusters. Yellow-flowered R. sphaerocarpa, rather than white-flowered R. monosperma.
plant_profile.growth_form: Airy shrub with arching, nearly leafless green shoots and small yellow flower clusters.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

esparto.label: Esparto
esparto.description: Robust tussock grass with long leaves that can roll into tubes. It forms dry grasslands known as espartales or atochares; this species identity is distinct from the habitat topic.
esparto.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Also known as Stipa tenacissima. Dense basal tussock of long, tough rolled leaves. Shown without flowers; flowering plants have slender stems with narrow panicles and awned spikelets.
plant_profile.growth_form: Dense basal tussock of rolled leaves with retained straw-coloured leaf bases; shown without flowers.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

thymus-hyemalis.label: Thyme
thymus-hyemalis.description: Low aromatic woody thyme with narrow rolled-margin leaves and pink flowers. The cited account concerns subsp. hyemalis in southeastern Iberian scrub and thyme communities.
thymus-hyemalis.name_note: Topic retains Thymus hyemalis; the principal detailed account is specifically subsp. hyemalis.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Small woody stems with tiny opposite, narrow rolled-margin leaves; compact terminal heads of pink, two-lipped flowers. The poster specifies winter thyme.
plant_profile.growth_form: Low woody subshrub forming a compact twiggy mound with small pink flower heads.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

rosemary.label: Rosemary
rosemary.description: Evergreen upright aromatic shrub with opposite narrow leaves, recurved margins and pale felted undersides. UAM records Rosmarinus officinalis and Salvia rosmarinus as synonyms.
rosemary.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Also called Rosmarinus officinalis. Opposite narrow leaves have rolled-under edges, dark green upper surfaces and whitish undersides. Small pale blue-lavender, two-lipped flowers sit near the stems; this is rosemary, not lavender.
plant_profile.growth_form: Upright branching evergreen shrub with narrow leaves; shown in an unpruned form.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

ephedra-fragilis.label: Joint pine
ephedra-fragilis.description: Much-branched shrub with articulated green shoots and tiny reduced leaves. Male and female plants are separate; the illustration depicts a female form. The UAL account concerns subsp. fragilis.
ephedra-fragilis.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Dense, slender green jointed stems with tiny scale-like leaves at the nodes and older grey woody branches. The depicted female sprig bears small red fleshy seed-cone bracts; these are not ordinary fruits or flowers. Male and female structures occur on separate plants.
plant_profile.growth_form: Much-branched shrub with jointed green shoots, tiny scales and older woody stems; female form shown.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

ziziphus-lotus.label: Ziziphus
ziziphus-lotus.description: Strongly thorny deciduous shrub forming dense rounded masses, with zigzag branches and three-veined leaves. Distinct from cultivated Ziziphus jujuba.
ziziphus-lotus.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

source_refs.locator: PDF 1: names, description, ecology and shelter/soil functions

plant_profile.identifying_features: Zigzag thorny shoots; alternate small oval leaves with three strong veins from the base and a finely scalloped margin; small drupes. This is wild Z. lotus, not cultivated Z. jujuba.
plant_profile.growth_form: Broad densely intertwined thorny shrub with a rounded, spreading crown.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

lycium-intricatum.label: Lycium
lycium-intricatum.description: Thorny shrub with twisted branches, fleshy grey-green leaves and violet tubular flowers. The university account associates it with warm rocky coastal sites.
lycium-intricatum.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Tortuous thorny branches, small fleshy grey-green leaves and violet tubular flowers with a flared mouth. The illustration represents the poster’s Mediterranean boxthorn.
plant_profile.growth_form: Low irregular shrub with tortuous thorny branches and small fleshy leaves.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

salsola-webbii.label: Salsola
salsola-webbii.description: Shrub of semi-arid scrub recorded in the UAL flora table for Almería and the Alpujarras. Kew accepts Salsola webbii and records southern Spain and Morocco as its native range.
salsola-webbii.name_note: Retain Salsola webbii. Kew qualifies Salsola ericoides as not validly published and Anabasis tamariscifolia as sensu auct.; these aliases do not establish unrestricted name equivalence.

source_refs.locator: PDF 66, printed 65: focused review of Salsola webbii and Thymus hyemalis rows; Tamarix species not generalized to an unidentified plant

plant_profile.identifying_features: Pale woody branches with very slender, curved, cylindrical grey-green leaves, alternate or in small axillary tufts. Shown in non-flowering foliage state, without broad flat blades. The poster uses the name Salsola webbii.
plant_profile.growth_form: Rounded to upright shrub with pale woody branches and very slender curved leaves; foliage state.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

oleander.label: Oleander
oleander.description: Evergreen shrub with narrow leathery leaves and terminal pink flower clusters. Occurs in non-saline wet places including ramblas; toxic if ingested.
oleander.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Long leathery lanceolate leaves, opposite or in whorls, with a strong midrib; terminal clusters of simple five-lobed pink flowers.
plant_profile.growth_form: Upright multistem shrub with narrow evergreen leaves and terminal flower clusters.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

tamarix.label: Tamarix (tree form)
tamarix.description: Genus-level tamarisk topic. The university habitat account records several Tamarix species with oleander in warm Mediterranean watercourse vegetation; the pictured taxon is not identified to species.
tamarix.name_note: Tamarix spp. intentionally remains genus-level. A T. gallica botanical illustration reference is an example, not an identification.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Fine branching twigs with tiny overlapping scale leaves and slender racemes of minute pink flowers. Genus-level representation: the poster does not identify a Tamarix species. The linked T. gallica describes an example, not the confirmed planting identity.
plant_profile.growth_form: Representative tree form with a loose crown and fine branchlets; Tamarix species can also be shrubby.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

semi-arid-shrubland.description: Semi-arid shrub vegetation; source-specific memberships retain their own context.

seasonal-watercourse.description: Warm Mediterranean rambla vegetation described with oleander and several Tamarix species.

coastal-rocky-scrub.description: Rocky coastal habitat described for Lycium intricatum.

rosemary-scrub.description: Romerales described in the Tabernas landscape.

sad-life-source.label: SAD (LIFE maintenance wording)
sad-life-source.description: The maintenance passage uses SAD for a fog-water tank system that releases about 15 L/plant/event when full, at a reported interval of about three weeks. The acronym is not expanded there. A correspondence with the AFDS mechanism is curated, not a verified expansion.

carob-community-almeria.label: Carob communities in Almería
carob-community-almeria.description: Regional examples of carob-associated vegetation in arid and semiarid Almería. Mastic and wild olive are observed at La Alcantarilla and La Tórtola; wider MR2 companions and potential habitats have different evidence. Las Labores is a managed restoration planting replacing almond and olive. These are explanatory regional groupings, not a single formal association.

cornical-scrub.label: Cornical scrub
cornical-scrub.description: Cornicales are named among the arid settings in the MR2 discussion. This habitat label alone does not establish a particular species identification or its occurrence at a finca.

carob-restoration-mr1.label: Carob restoration of degraded areas (MR1)
carob-restoration-mr1.description: MR1 uses carob with other forest species for soil protection and restoration of degraded Mediterranean areas. Restoration layouts, genetic diversity and microsite selection differ from production-oriented plantings.

carob-diversification-mr3.label: Carob landscape diversification (MR3)
carob-diversification-mr3.description: The introductory passage describes diversification of low-productivity agricultural landscapes, particularly olive and almond areas, where carob can occur with other forest species and xerophytic shrubs. Only the opening on page 137 is covered here.
